title: Making the Platform Searchable by People
description: 2026-04-13. I am working on the enterprise content hierarchy, ingestion pipeline, search interface, project filtering, and tool wiring completed across April 12.
body:
2026-04-13. I am working on the enterprise content hierarchy, ingestion pipeline, search interface, project filtering, and tool wiring completed across April 12.

At this point, the service becomes easier to inspect when the data model, ingestion path, and human-facing search experience meet in one inspectable operating model. The immediate objective is to make explicit what enters the system, what is recorded about it, and what remains outside the claim being made.

Why this matters

The implementation is deliberately concrete. this is a working presentation layer, not the end of the platform; it gives users and agents a concrete place to ask whether the knowledge model is returning evidence that deserves trust. This is why the work includes service contracts, stored records, and repeatable operations rather than a single broad description of “AI memory.” Each layer needs a job that can be inspected.

The implementation does not replace the judgment required to describe a business, a document set, or a working team. It provides a repeatable path for retaining the evidence that judgment uses. A technical decision is useful only when a later reader can see its scope, its constraints, and the result it was intended to support.

What I will test next

The next work will test that operating model in actual practice: whether the records can be retrieved at the right time, whether their provenance remains clear, and whether the system makes a real task easier without overstating what it knows. That distinction will guide the outcome posts that follow.

Historical basis: This entry is dated to the 2026-04-13 repository milestone, commits 2b1f25e, a1be388, d03abd9, c55d9f1. It is based on the contemporaneous implementation records and their documented scope.
